enonce_intro_markdown: A car travels on a straight horizontal track. The car decelerates uniformly from a speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ to a speed of $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ as it travels a distance of $640\ \mathrm{m}$. The car then accelerates uniformly, travelling a further $1820\ \mathrm{m}$ in $70\ \mathrm{s}$. Calculate the
incertitudes: Question 2 : le sujet n'imprime pas de valeur de g ; elle n'intervient pas (piste horizontale, mouvements à accélération constante).

questions.enonce_markdown: time that it takes the car to travel the first $640\ \mathrm{m}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Straight-line motion in the direction of travel (positive), with constant acceleration in each phase. First phase: $u = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $v = 12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $s = 640\ \mathrm{m}$.

With constant acceleration the distance is the average speed times the time: $s = \tfrac12(u + v)\,t$.

$$640 = \tfrac12(20 + 12)\,t = 16\,t \;\Rightarrow\; t = \frac{640}{16} = 40\ \mathrm{s}$$

**Time $= 40\ \mathrm{s}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: deceleration of the car during the first $640\ \mathrm{m}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 20$, $v = 12$, $s = 640$ (positive direction = direction of travel):

$$12^2 = 20^2 + 2a(640) \;\Rightarrow\; 144 = 400 + 1280\,a \;\Rightarrow\; a = -\frac{256}{1280} = -0.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

(Check with part (a): $v = u + at = 20 - 0.2\times 40 = 12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.)

**The deceleration is $0.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: acceleration of the car as it travels the further $1820\ \mathrm{m}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Second phase: the car starts at $u = 12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (the speed at the end of the first phase), $s = 1820\ \mathrm{m}$, $t = 70\ \mathrm{s}$. Use $s = ut + \tfrac12 a t^2$:

$$1820 = 12(70) + \tfrac12 a (70)^2 = 840 + 2450\,a \;\Rightarrow\; a = \frac{980}{2450} = 0.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**The acceleration is $0.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$** (in the direction of travel).

questions.enonce_markdown: speed of the car when it has completed the further $1820\ \mathrm{m}$,
average speed of the car as it travels the $2460\ \mathrm{m}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The total distance is $640 + 1820 = 2460\ \mathrm{m}$ and the total time is $40 + 70 = 110\ \mathrm{s}$. Average speed is total distance divided by total time (it is not the mean of $20$ and $40$, because the two phases last different times):

$$\text{average speed} = \frac{2460}{110} = \frac{246}{11} \approx 22.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

**Average speed $\approx 22.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**
